claims.text: Ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder has potential oxygen contamination.
Sintering at 900–1000 °C triggers kinetic phase separation in Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co.
The phase separation produces Ti/V-rich Laves or B2-type phases at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
The Ti/V-rich secondary phases act as barriers to cation transport during oxidation.
Temperatures below 800 °C provide insufficient activation energy for the proposed precipitation.
Temperatures above 1000 °C cause substantial Mg evaporation and composition deviation.
SPS at 950 °C for 10–30 minutes permits grain growth while limiting Mg loss.
High-temperature SPS decomposes the metastable BCC solid solution into a dual-phase microstructure.
Secondary-phase precipitation reduces atomic-radius misfit and the elastic energy of the solid solution.
The secondary phases pin grain boundaries and refine the microstructure.
The secondary phases and refined grain-boundary network promote rapid outward diffusion of Cr and Ti.
Outward diffusion forms a dense, continuous, adherent Cr2O3/TiO2 scale that limits further oxygen ingress.
Coarse-grained or under-sintered material forms non-protective spinel scales.
The optimized alloy will attain more than 98% theoretical density.
The optimized alloy will attain Vickers hardness above 600 HV through grain refinement and precipitation hardening.
The 950 °C material will have a substantially lower parabolic oxidation rate constant than material sintered below 800 °C or above 1000 °C.
Material sintered below 800 °C remains porous and single-phase BCC and has poor oxidation resistance.
Mg loss above 1000 °C prevents formation of the Ti/V-rich phases required for barrier formation.
Argon or vacuum minimizes oxygen intake during both milling and sintering.

contradictions.description: The stated alloy contains Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co but no Cr, yet the proposed mechanism, predicted passive film, and falsification rule require outward Cr diffusion and a Cr-rich or Cr2O3-containing scale.

The Ti/V-rich phases are described as barriers to cation transport, but the same phases are also said to facilitate rapid outward transport of Ti and Cr; no species-selective or path-specific explanation reconciles these opposing transport roles.
The alloy explicitly lists six elements, whereas the uncertainty field calls it a quinary system.
